# nonCountable

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a countable number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonCountable() — Checks whether a value is **not** a countable number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonCountable<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonCountable(value)` is the same test as `!isCountable(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

A value that can serve as a quantity, a length or a zero-based index: a whole number, not negative, and small enough that integer arithmetic on it is still exact.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a countable number; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonCountable(-1); // => true
nonCountable(1.5); // => true
nonCountable(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // => true
nonCountable(0); // => false
nonCountable(42); // => false
```
